name: Dose Dialogue
description: Illustrated pharmacy consultation deck with object prompts, action routes and editable service infographics.

slides.title: Questions make the consultation useful
items: A pharmacy conversation starts with the person’s questions and a clear record of what they currently use.
Arrange a consultation, record the agreed actions and make the follow-up contact visible to the person and the team.

slides.title: A useful record has four parts
items: Record what the person reports using, including non-prescription products.
Capture concerns in the person’s own words before the discussion.
Document the advice or referral agreed with the pharmacist.
Record who will make contact and when the next review is due.

slides.title: Objects can prompt the right questions
items: Helps the conversation identify the product being discussed.
Provides a starting point to check with the pharmacist.
Keep the person’s questions and agreed next steps together.

slides.title: Five stages keep the discussion focused
items: Agree the purpose and what the person wants to discuss.
Check the information available and clarify any gaps.
The pharmacist responds to the person’s questions.
Record the next action and the responsible person.
Confirm how the next contact will happen.
Clinical advice and referrals follow the pharmacy’s approved practice.

slides.title: The action can take different routes
items: The pharmacist records the answer and checks understanding.
The record identifies the receiving service and how the handover will be confirmed.

slides.title: A follow-up is a planned conversation
items: The person knows who will contact them and the purpose of the call.
The team reviews the previous actions, records the discussion and agrees any further contact with the person.

slides.title: The pilot follows 80 consultations
items: Appointment agreed and awaiting the conversation.
A named team member owns the next attempt.
Synthetic status snapshot. Categories sum to 80.

slides.title: Understanding is worth measuring
items: Repeat the same question across review rounds. Record how many people replied so the team can interpret the result.

slides.title: The record travels with the action
items: The record captures the concern as the person describes it.
The pharmacist records the discussion and the agreed next step.
A named role tracks the action until it is resolved or handed over.
The team records whether the handover has reached its destination.

slides.title: A small team needs clear ownership
items: Owns the consultation, clinical advice and referral decisions within the service.
Owns booking, contact attempts and the list of unresolved follow-up actions.
The team checks outstanding actions, appointment capacity and incomplete records.

slides.title: The pilot learns before it grows
items: Agree documentation and rehearse the handover with sample records.
Open the initial appointment slots and review unresolved actions weekly.
Compare completed contacts, patient understanding and staff workload.
The expansion decision uses the pilot record and locally agreed service requirements.

slides.title: A £120k pilot funds the whole pathway
items: Pharmacist time and supervised service training.
Booking, contact attempts and follow-up administration.
Record review, patient feedback and rollout planning.
Illustrative three-month budget. Allocations sum to £120k.
